column4: The implementation of GHG reduction targets can reinforce the achievement of GHG removal targets by creating a synergistic effect, where reducing emissions can also enhance carbon sinks and removals.
Reducing GHG emissions can enable waste reduction by decreasing energy consumption and promoting sustainable practices, which in turn can lead to a decrease in waste generation.

Implementing GHG reduction targets can facilitate the transition to a circular economy by promoting sustainable consumption and production patterns, which can lead to increased recycling and reuse of materials.

The extraction and import of critical raw materials required for low-carbon technologies can constrain GHG reduction efforts by generating emissions and environmental impacts associated with extraction and processing.
Improving energy efficiency in buildings can enable waste reduction in municipal waste management by promoting sustainable practices and reducing energy consumption.
Promoting low-emission transportation can facilitate food waste reduction by decreasing energy consumption and promoting sustainable food systems.
The implementation of GHG removal targets can counteract waste reduction efforts by generating emissions and environmental impacts associated with the production and use of removal technologies.

Implementing waste reduction targets can be inextricably linked to the transition to a circular economy, as reducing waste generation and increasing recycling can lead to a significant decrease in emissions and environmental impacts.

Reducing municipal waste can be inextricably linked to increasing recycling and reuse of materials, as it enables the transition to a circular economy and promotes sustainable waste management practices.
Reducing food waste can facilitate the recycling and reuse of textile waste by promoting sustainable consumption patterns and reducing the environmental impacts associated with textile production.

Reducing plastic waste and increasing recycling can be inextricably linked to the transition to a circular economy, as it enables the reduction of emissions and environmental impacts associated with plastic production and use.

The transition to a circular economy can counteract critical raw material extraction and import by promoting sustainable consumption patterns and reducing waste generation, which can lead to a decrease in demand for primary raw materials.
The extraction and import of critical raw materials can enable the manufacturing of net-zero technologies by providing the necessary materials for their production.
